description: Rigorous synthetic-data study of the BKT slip probability P(S) for the Sanskrit AI Tutor. Pure research: no production constant, schema, endpoint, learner record or UI is modified by this experiment.

population.lesson_sampling: distinct lessons drawn from the real 25-lesson catalog; the learner's own tier is upweighted

split.note: Split by STUDENT identity so a learner's response history can never straddle partitions.

slip_grid.note: 0.01..0.50 inclusive. P(S)=0.10 is the production value and lies on this grid; it is asserted at runtime rather than assumed.

metrics.note: Prediction metrics measure answer-prediction quality, NOT whether the true mastery state was identified. Mastery metrics are reported separately (see mastery_estimation).

mastery_estimation.note: False-mastery / false-unmastered rates are reported with explicit denominators. Hidden mastery labels exist ONLY because the data is synthetic; they are not measurable on real students.

bootstrap.note: Resampling whole students preserves within-sequence answer correlation.

dgp.comment: HIDDEN data-generating parameters - experimental assumptions, NOT measured properties of Sanskrit learners.
dgp.transition_mode_note: 'deterministic' grows hidden mastery regardless of the answer, so it is structurally misspecified for BKT (slip absorbs the mismatch). 'bkt_binary' is the canonical BKT HMM, under which the fitted model is exactly correct.
dgp.observation_model: deterministic: p(correct)=theta*(1-s)+(1-theta)*g ; theta<-theta+(1-theta)*t | bkt_binary: Z~Bernoulli(l0) ; y|Z : P(correct|Z=1)=1-s, P(correct|Z=0)=g ; Z<-Z OR Bernoulli(t)
dgp.note: The production parameterisation (t=0.15, g=0.25, s=0.10, l0=INITIAL_MASTERY) is the default DGP because it is the natural null hypothesis for 'is the production slip plausible?'.

hypotheses.H1: Prediction and mastery-estimation metrics change measurably as P(S) changes.
hypotheses.H2: The configured production P(S) may or may not be near-optimal under the synthetic DGP.
hypotheses.H3: When data are generated with a known slip and other parameters are correctly specified, fitting recovers that slip or a justified near-optimal interval.
hypotheses.H4: Incorrect assumptions about P(G), P(L0) or P(T) shift the estimated slip value.
hypotheses.H5: Multiple slip values may be statistically indistinguishable - the data may not identify a unique optimum.
hypotheses.note: Pre-registered before results were inspected. Findings are reported even when they contradict these expectations.

variants.interpretation: THE FAIR TEST: the canonical BKT HMM with a near-point prior, so the fitted model is exactly the generating model. Slip should be recoverable here if it is recoverable anywhere.
Point prior but deterministic (answer-independent) learning. Isolates the structural misspecification of the deterministic transition on its own.
The sibling prior experiment's DGP: Beta-distributed initial mastery AND answer-independent learning. This is the realistic-but-structurally-misspecified case.

experiment_b.label: Recovery of known generating slip values

variants.interpretation: All other parameters genuinely correct and the model exactly specified - the ONLY condition under which H3 (recovery) is a fair test.
Correct point prior but answer-independent learning, exposing how much slip bias the transition mismatch alone creates.
Adds Beta-distributed initial mastery on top, showing how much extra bias unmodelled heterogeneity contributes.

experiment_b.note: Includes low, medium, high and boundary-ish values to expose identifiability limits.

experiment_c.label: Parameter-confounding analysis
experiment_c.sd_note: Experiment C uses the canonical BKT HMM with a near-deterministic spread so that confounding between g, l0 and s is measured cleanly, without structural misspecification or heterogeneity also pushing the slip estimate.

conditions.label: 6. Initial mastery and slip jointly fitted
7. Guess, initial mastery and slip jointly fitted (t fixed)
8. Combined misspecification (g, t and l0 all wrong)

experiment_d.label: Heterogeneous learners and skills
experiment_d.transition_note: The canonical BKT HMM is used so that any fitted-slip shift reflects genuine heterogeneity across cells, not the deterministic-transition bias isolated in Experiment B.

conditions.label: Slip varies by difficulty tier (easy 0.05 / intermediate 0.10 / advanced 0.15)
Slip varies by learner proficiency (beg 0.15 / int 0.10 / adv 0.05)

experiment_d.note: The single fitted slip is judged against per-tier / per-group truth. Synthetic group differences are NOT evidence that real learners behave this way.
